qe:
Select the part that contains an error:
'The performance (A) / of our players (B) / was worst than (C) / I had expected (D).'
qh:
उस भाग का चयन करें जिसमें त्रुटि है:
'The performance (A) / of our players (B) / was worst than (C) / I had expected (D).'
e: For comparison between two states (expected vs actual), we use the comparative degree 'worse' instead of the superlative 'worst'.

qe: The Captain said to the soldiers, 'Don't move from your posts.'
qh: The Captain said to the soldiers, 'Don't move from your posts.'
oe: The Captain ordered the soldiers not to move from their posts
The Captain told the soldiers that don't move
The Captain commanded the soldiers to not move
The Captain asked the soldiers no moving
oh: The Captain ordered the soldiers not to move from their posts
The Captain told the soldiers that don't move
The Captain commanded the soldiers to not move
The Captain asked the soldiers no moving
e: Negative imperative sentences use 'ordered/commanded + not to + V1'. 'Your' changes to 'their' to match the object.

qe: 'The manager decided to ______ the meeting until next Monday.'
qh: 'The manager decided to ______ the meeting until next Monday.'
e: 'Put off' means to postpone. 'Put out' means to extinguish.

qe: 'A person who is fluent in two languages.'
qh: 'वह व्यक्ति जो दो भाषाओं में धाराप्रवाह हो।'
e: Bilingual (द्विभाषी) is the term for someone who can speak two languages fluently.

qe: 'Hardly <u>had the sun rose</u> when the birds started chirping.'
qh: 'Hardly <u>had the sun rose</u> when the birds started chirping.'
e: With 'had', the third form of the verb (V3) is used. The V3 of rise is risen (Rise-Rose-Risen).

qe: Select the most appropriate synonym of: 'TACITURN'
e: Taciturn means reserved or uncommunicative in speech. Reticent is its closest synonym.

qe: Select the most appropriate antonym of: 'ZENITH'
e: Zenith means the highest point. Nadir (पाताल/न्यूनतम बिंदु) means the lowest point.

qe: 'To hold one's tongue.'
e: To refrain from speaking or to stay silent.

qe: 'Who painted this beautiful picture?'
oe: By whom was this beautiful picture painted?
Who was this picture painted by?
By whom this picture was painted?
oh: By whom was this beautiful picture painted?
Who was this picture painted by?
By whom this picture was painted?
e: 'Who' changes to 'By whom' or 'Who...by'. Simple Past (V2) changes to 'was/were + V3'.

qe: 'The cost (A) / of living (B) / is higher than (C) / the last year (D).'
qh: 'The cost (A) / of living (B) / is higher than (C) / the last year (D).'
e: Faulty comparison. We must compare the 'cost' of this year with the 'cost' of last year. Correct: 'higher than that of last year'.

qe: Select the correctly spelled word.
e: Hierarchy is the correct spelling.

qe: 'If you ______ the instructions, you wouldn't have made these mistakes.'
qh: 'If you ______ the instructions, you wouldn't have made these mistakes.'
e: Type 3 Conditional follows the pattern: 'If + had + V3, would have + V3'.

qe: 'To play second fiddle.'
oe: To be in a subordinate position
oh: To be in a subordinate position
e: To take a less important or subordinate role compared to someone else.

qe: 'Not only the students (A) / but also the teacher (B) / were happy (C) / with the results (D).'
qh: 'Not only the students (A) / but also the teacher (B) / were happy (C) / with the results (D).'
e: For 'Not only...but also', the verb agrees with the nearest subject. 'The teacher' is singular, so it should be 'was'.

qe: 'A small boy was flying a colorful kite.'
qh: 'A small boy was flying a colorful kite.'
oe: A colorful kite was being flown by a small boy
oh: A colorful kite was being flown by a small boy
e: Past Continuous changes to 'was/were + being + V3' (Fly-Flew-Flown).

qe: Antonym of 'BENEVOLENT'.
e: Benevolent means kind. Malevolent (द्रोही/बुरा चाहने वाला) means having a wish to do evil.

qe: 'A person who hates mankind.'
qh: 'वह व्यक्ति जो मानव जाति से घृणा करता है।'
e: Misanthrope (मानवद्वेषी) is the correct term. Philanthropist is the opposite.

qe: 'The news <u>was too good being true</u>.'
e: The structure is 'Too + Adjective + To + V1'.

qe: He asked me, 'Where do you live?'
qh: He asked me, 'Where do you live?'
oe: He asked me where I lived
He asked me where did I live
He asked me where I live
He asked where was my home
oh: He asked me where I lived
He asked me where did I live
He asked me where I live
He asked where was my home
e: In indirect questions, the sentence becomes assertive (Subject + Verb). Simple Present changes to Simple Past.

qe: 'You must dispense ______ his services.'
e: 'Dispense with' means to stop using or get rid of something.

qe: 'Shut all the doors.'
oe: Let all the doors be shut
oh: Let all the doors be shut
e: Imperative passive starts with 'Let + object + be + V3'.

qe: Synonym of 'AFFLUENT'.
e: Affluent means having a great deal of money or wealthy.

qe: 'He is senior (A) / than me (B) / in service (C) / No error (D).'
qh: 'He is senior (A) / than me (B) / in service (C) / No error (D).'
e: 'Senior' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'.

qe: 'To bite the dust.'
e: To fail or be defeated, often in a humiliating way.

qe: Correct spelling of 'Maintanance'.
e: The correct spelling is Maintenance.

qe: Antonym of 'ARTIFICIAL'.
e: The opposite of artificial (कृत्रिम) is Natural (प्राकृतिक).

qe: 'I prefer tea ______ coffee.'
e: The verb 'prefer' takes 'to' for comparison between two nouns.

qe: 'A collection of poems.'
e: Anthology is the specific word for a collection of literary works.

qe: 'If I <u>am</u> you, I wouldn't forgive him.'
qh: 'If I <u>am</u> you, I wouldn't forgive him.'
e: For hypothetical/imaginary situations, 'were' is used with all subjects.

qe: 'The jury (A) / were (B) / unanimous (C) / in its decision (D).'
qh: 'The jury (A) / were (B) / unanimous (C) / in its decision (D).'
e: When a collective noun acts as a single unit (unanimous), it takes a singular verb ('was').

qe: My mother said, 'Honesty is the best policy.'
qh: My mother said, 'Honesty is the best policy.'
oe: My mother said that honesty is the best policy
My mother said that honesty was the best policy
My mother told honesty is the best policy
oh: My mother said that honesty is the best policy
My mother said that honesty was the best policy
My mother told honesty is the best policy
e: Tense does not change for Proverbs/Universal Truths.

qe: 'He died ______ cholera.'
e: 'Die of' is used for diseases.

qe: 'To let the cat out of the bag.'
qh: 'To let the cat out of the bag.'
e: To reveal a secret, usually by mistake.

qe: 'They are laughing at the poor man.'
qh: 'They are laughing at the poor man.'
oe: The poor man is being laughed at by them
oh: The poor man is being laughed at by them
e: Present Continuous passive: 'is/am/are + being + V3'. Don't forget the preposition 'at'.

qe: Synonym of 'CANDID'.
e: Candid means honest and straightforward, or Frank.
